newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA cuts key housing rate to 6.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA cuts key housing rate to 6.8 pct.

text.p: The Commonwealth Bank of Australia said on Wednesday that it would cut its standard variable mortgage rate to 6.8 percent from 7.2 percent in response to the central bank's latest monetary policy easing.

The bank, one of Australia's big four and with one of the largest mortgage portfolios, said the new rate on its standard package would apply to new customers from July 31 and to existing customers from September 22.
It said the rate on its no-frills "economiser" mortgage rate would be reduced to 6.35 percent from 6.7 percent.

CBA is the first bank to cut rates in response to the 50 basis point cash easing announced by the Reserve Bank in its 9.30 a.m. (02330 GMT) morning statement. The standard rates of other major banks Westpac Banking Corp and National Australia Bank Ltd are at 7.2 percent.
Another major bank, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, has a standard rate of 6.99 percent. It said it may make an announcement later on Wednesday.
Mortgage originator Aussie Home Loans said it would cut its fixed rate by the full 50 basis points to 6.49 percent.
The Australian treasurer Peter Costello was critical of the major banks when they did not pass on the full 50 basis point easing when the central bank eased on May 23.
